manuscript_prose.section1_title: Evolutionary Transition from Asgardarchaeota to the Compartmentalized Eukaryotic Nucleus
manuscript_prose.section1_p1: The origin of the membrane-bound nucleus represents the defining cellular divide between prokaryotic archaea and the Last Eukaryotic Common Ancestor (LECA). Closed and open nuclear envelopes decouple RNA polymerase II transcription and spliceosomal intron removal inside a protected nucleoplasm from cytosolic translation on 80S ribosomes, preventing aberrant translation of unspliced pre-mRNA introns while organizing chromosomes onto octameric histone arrays.
manuscript_prose.section1_p2: Across 64 taxa spanning Euryarchaeota outgroups [A], TACK Proteoarchaeota [B], complete Asgardarchaeota genomes [C] (Promethearchaeum, Lokiarchaeum, Flexarchaeum, Margulisarchaeum, Odinarchaeum, and Heimdallarchaeum), and crown eukaryotic supergroups [D]-[G], partitioned ModelTest and Dual-Pass Blinded validation trace three integrated functional pillars: (1) Asgard ESCRT-III and VPS4 ATPase endomembrane scaffolding, (2) Nuclear Pore Complex coatomer architecture powered by the Ran-GTPase (1BYU) nucleocytoplasmic gradient, and (3) histone H3 chromatin compaction paired with RNAP II RPB2 transcriptional compartmentalization.
manuscript_prose.section2_title: Per-Locus BIC ModelTest, Third-Codon RY3 Compositional De-Biasing & Proterozoic Chronogram
manuscript_prose.section3_title: 64-Species Quartet Multispecies Coalescent, Eocyte-Hodarchaeia/Heimdallarchaeia Root & ABBA-BABA Tests
manuscript_prose.section4_title: ESCRT-III VPS4 Scaffolding, Histone H3 Chromatin, RNAP II RPB2 & Ran-GTPase (1BYU) Dynamics
manuscript_prose.section4_body: Across four nuclear-origin functional gene families under Standard Genetic Code 1, 61-state Goldman-Yang codon models quantify purifying selection maintaining the AAA+ ATPase pore of ESCRT-III disassembly factor VPS4 (FAM-01), core nucleosomal Histone H3 (FAM-02), and the active cleft of RNA polymerase II RPB2 (FAM-03). Alongside these three compartments, nuclear transport master GTPase RAN/GSP1 (FAM-04) is threaded onto the 2.15 A crystal structure of GDP-bound Ran (PDB 1BYU Chain A), preserving the Walker A P-loop (GDGGTGKT), Switch II hydrolysis loop (DTAGQE), and octahedral Mg2+ A 221 coordination via Thr24 Og1 that establishes directional nucleocytoplasmic import and export across LECA nuclear pores.
manuscript_prose.section5_title: Single-Species Archaeal & Eukaryotic Skylines (Code 1/11 vs. SSU 18S rRNA) & Stage 3C Clusters
manuscript_prose.abstract_context: Understanding how the eukaryotic nucleus emerged from archaeal ancestors requires resolving deep archaeal-eukaryotic relationships alongside the evolutionary conservation of nuclear transport, chromatin, and membrane-remodeling machinery.
manuscript_prose.executive_summary_lead: traces the origin of the eukaryotic nucleus from Asgardarchaeota to crown eukaryotes
discussion_paragraphs: **Two-Domain Phylogenomics and Cross-Domain Compositional Bias.** Reconstructing relationships across Archaea and Eukaryota requires disentangling genuine phylogenetic signal from convergent nucleotide and amino-acid composition driven by thermal adaptation and genomic GC drift [4, 23]. Across our 64-taxon dataset, edge-linked per-locus rate partitioning [14, 15] combined with third-codon purine–pyrimidine recoding eliminated 83.6% of cross-domain compositional heterogeneity (reducing RCFV from 0.1440 unrecoded and 0.1558 unfiltered to 0.0236) and yielded a +8,013.3 log-likelihood improvement over unpartitioned concatenation [1]. Under both partitioned maximum likelihood and 18-locus quartet coalescent reconciliation (Q = 0.73, mean local posterior probability = 0.81) [17], Asgardarchaeota is recovered as the monophyletic sister lineage to crown Eukaryota nested alongside TACK Proteoarchaeota relative to Euryarchaeota outgroups, corroborating two-domain eocyte and Asgard topologies over classical three-domain rooting [2–4, 23]. Quartet concordance and four-taxon Patterson's *D* contrasts [19] further indicate that while core eukaryotic clades such as Opisthokonta, Embryophyta, Dictyostelia, and SAR are robustly supported, deep internodes separating Discoba, Amoebozoa, Obazoa, and Diaphoretickes retain substantial gene-tree conflict consistent with rapid Paleoproterozoic diversification and ancestral incomplete lineage sorting [4, 24].

**Geological Context of the FECA-to-LECA Stem Interval.** Our relaxed-clock chronology [16] places the divergence between Asgardarchaeota and the First Eukaryotic Common Ancestor (FECA) stem in the Neoarchean at 2.93 Ga (95% HPD: 2.57–3.20 Ga) and the crown radiation of extant eukaryotic supergroups (LECA) in the Paleoproterozoic at 1.85 Ga (95% HPD: 1.59–2.11 Ga), followed by Mesoproterozoic–Phanerozoic diversification across major clades including SAR (1.40 Ga), Dikarya Fungi (1.35 Ga), Dictyostelia (1.10 Ga), and Embryophyta (0.56 Ga) [12, 13, 24]. These intervals align closely with multigene molecular-clock syntheses placing LECA between ~1.9 and 1.6 Ga [12, 24] and predating diagnostic Mesoproterozoic eukaryotic microfossils, including ornamented organic-walled acritarchs (*Shuiyousphaeridium*, *Tappania*) at ~1.65–1.45 Ga [25] and multicellular red algae (*Bangiomorpha pubescens*) dated to 1.047 Ga [26]. Crucially, the ~1.08-billion-year stem separating FECA from LECA spans Earth's Paleoproterozoic Great Oxidation Event (~2.43–2.22 Ga) [27]. As rising surface oxygenation restructured marine and benthic redox gradients [27], syntrophic metabolic consortia between anaerobic, H<sub>2</sub>-evolving Asgard archaea—analogous to cultured *Promethearchaeum syntrophicum* [5]—and facultatively aerobic alphaproteobacteria would have experienced strong ecological pressure for intimate membrane contact, metabolic channeling, and eventual mitochondrial endosymbiosis [4, 5, 10].

**Stepwise Assembly of the Nuclear Envelope, Chromatin, and Ran-Gated Transport.** Codon substitution models [18] and structural homology threading across VPS4, Histone H3, RPB2, and RAN support a modular, stepwise assembly of the nuclear compartment rather than a single saltational invention [8–10]. Prokaryotic precursors for three of these systems already existed in Asgard and TACK archaea: Cdv/ESCRT-III polymers coupled to VPS4 AAA+ ATPases mediated membrane scission and extracellular protrusion dynamics [2, 6]; minimal archaeal histones wrapped DNA into hypernucleosomal arrays lacking extended epigenetic tails [21]; and multisubunit archaeal RNA polymerases shared homologous catalytic clefts with eukaryotic RNAP I–III [9]. Under either endomembrane-invagination models—in which COPII/NPC-like β-propeller/α-solenoid protocoatomers curved internal endomembranes around chromatin [8, 9]—or "inside-out" models—in which expanding extracellular archaeal blebs engulfed ectosymbiotic mitochondria and fused via ESCRT-III/VPS4 scission [5, 6, 10]—the proliferation of alphaproteobacterial group II introns into host genomes would have imposed acute selection for a physical barrier preventing ribosomes from translating unspliced transcripts [7].

**Frozen Functional Constraint Prior to Crown Radiation.** Once established in LECA, the molecular machinery of nuclear compartmentalization became locked under stringent purifying selection across all extant eukaryotic supergroups [9, 18]. Notably, core nucleosomal Histone H3 (M0 dN/dS = 0.031; 97.0% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.019) [21] and the Ran transport GTPase (M0 dN/dS = 0.031; 93.6% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.019) [11, 20] exhibit even tighter evolutionary constraint than the catalytic cleft of RNAP II RPB2 (dN/dS = 0.085) or the VPS4 disassembly ATPase (dN/dS = 0.101), with zero positively selected active-site codons across any of the four families. Structural superposition of eukaryotic RAN orthologs onto the 2.15 Å GDP-bound crystal structure (PDB 1BYU; TM-score = 0.978, Cα RMSD = 0.94 Å) [11] confirms complete invariance of the Walker A phosphate-binding P-loop (GDGGTGKT), the Switch II catalytic glutamine motif (DTAGQE), the NKVD guanine-recognition pocket, and the 2.32 Å octahedral Thr24 Oγ1–Mg<sup>2+</sup> coordination bond [11, 20]. Because a single Ran-GTPase switch simultaneously governs karyopherin cargo import/export during interphase and spindle assembly and nuclear-envelope reassembly after mitosis, compensatory drift within its nucleotide-binding pocket is strongly deleterious [9, 20].

**Intraspecific Baselines and Study Limitations.** Pairing deep phylogenomic inference with single-species coalescent analyses across representative archaeal and eukaryotic lineages illustrates how structural conservation at universal ribosomal, polymerase, and elongation-factor loci persists across broad variation in effective population size, ploidy, and reproductive mode [1]. Several limitations nevertheless bound these conclusions. First, our supermatrix focuses on 18 universal informational and core cellular markers to maintain cross-domain orthology, whereas finer resolution of the exact sister lineage within Heimdallarchaeia or Hodarchaeales benefits from broader sampling of Asgard-enriched accessory proteomes and uncultivated deep-sediment metagenomes [4, 6, 22]. Second, Archean and Paleoproterozoic relaxed-clock intervals remain inherently sensitive to deep branch-length saturation and the placement of maximum paleobiological calibration bounds [12, 13, 16]. Finally, static homology threading onto monomeric Ran-GDP (1BYU) captures active-site conservation [11] but does not directly model macromolecular conformational transitions across intact ~100 MDa Nuclear Pore Complexes or RanBP1/RCC1 co-complexes [8, 20].
manuscript_prose.latex_intro: Origin of the eukaryotic nucleus traced across Euryarchaeota, TACK Archaea, Asgardarchaeota, and four major eukaryotic supergroups via universal informational markers, VPS4/H3/RPB2/RAN codon selection, and 1BYU Ran-GDP structural threading.
manuscript_prose.abstract_override: The emergence of the membrane-bound nucleus—separating spliceosomal pre-mRNA processing and histone-packaged chromosomes from cytoplasmic translation—marks the foundational cellular transition from archaea to the Last Eukaryotic Common Ancestor (LECA). Although comparative genomics implicates Asgardarchaeota as the closest prokaryotic relatives of eukaryotes, extreme GC and thermophilic composition biases across billion-year branches continue to challenge deep archaeal–eukaryotic topology and divergence timing. Here, we analyze an 18-locus universal informational and core cellular supermatrix (26,387 aligned base pairs) across 64 archaeal and eukaryotic species spanning Euryarchaeota, TACK Proteoarchaeota, Asgardarchaeota, Discoba, Amoebozoa, Opisthokonta, Archaeplastida, and SAR, integrating per-locus model selection, third-codon purine–pyrimidine (RY) recoding, multispecies coalescent reconciliation across 5,880,795 gene-tree quartets, codon selection modeling, and 3D structural alignment. Partitioned modeling and RY recoding reduced cross-domain compositional heterogeneity by 83.6% (RCFV = 0.0236) and improved log-likelihood by +8,013.3 units over unpartitioned concatenation, recovering Asgardarchaeota as sister to crown Eukaryota with 95.1% mean bootstrap support across 52 completeness-gated taxa and strong gene-tree concordance across all 64 species (Q = 0.73). Relaxed-clock dating places the Asgard–eukaryote divergence in the Neoarchean at 2.93 Ga (95% HPD: 2.57–3.20 Ga) and the LECA crown radiation in the Paleoproterozoic at 1.85 Ga (95% HPD: 1.59–2.11 Ga), framing an extended stem interval spanning the Great Oxidation Event. Across 47 eukaryotic orthologs of VPS4, Histone H3, RPB2, and RAN, codon models reveal intense purifying selection (dN/dS = 0.031–0.101), while structural threading onto GDP-bound Ran (PDB 1BYU; TM-score = 0.978, RMSD = 0.94 Å) demonstrates invariant active-site geometry entrenching directional nucleocytoplasmic transport prior to crown supergroup diversification.
section1_paragraphs: The origin of the eukaryotic nucleus represents one of the most consequential organizational transitions in the history of life [7, 9]. Unlike prokaryotic cells, in which nascent transcripts are translated co-transcriptionally by ribosomes directly on exposed chromosomes, eukaryotic cells enclose linear, nucleosome-compacted chromosomes within a double-membrane nuclear envelope perforated by octagonal Nuclear Pore Complexes (NPCs) [8, 9, 21]. This spatial barrier decouples DNA-directed RNA polymerase II transcription and spliceosomal intron excision in the nucleoplasm from 80S ribosomal translation in the cytosol—preventing premature translation of unspliced pre-mRNAs after group II intron proliferation while enabling complex post-transcriptional regulation [7]. Directional traffic of ribonucleoproteins, histones, and polymerases across the nuclear envelope depends on a steep chemical gradient of the small Ras-superfamily GTPase Ran, maintained between chromatin-tethered guanine nucleotide exchange factors (RCC1) inside the nucleus and GTPase-activating proteins (RanGAP) on cytoplasmic pore filaments [9, 11, 20].

Over the past decade, metagenomic assemblies and syntrophic enrichments of Asgardarchaeota—including *Promethearchaeum syntrophicum*, *Candidatus* Lokiarchaeum, Odinarchaeia, Hodarchaeales, and Heimdallarchaeia—have reshaped two-domain models of eukaryogenesis [2–6, 23]. Asgard genomes encode an extensive repertoire of eukaryotic signature proteins (ESPs), including profilin-regulated actin filaments, tubulin homologs, ubiquitin-modifier pathways, and ESCRT-III/VPS4 membrane-scission ATPases capable of supporting branched extracellular protrusions and vesicle remodeling before the acquisition of a closed nuclear envelope [2, 3, 6, 22]. Resolving the exact phylogenetic and temporal bridge between extremophilic archaea and mesophilic eukaryotes nevertheless remains technically demanding: hyperthermophilic TACK and Euryarchaeota lineages exhibit strong purine-loading and GC-biased substitution regimes that induce long-branch attraction and artificial root placements under homogeneous substitution matrices, while uneven gene retention and ancient incomplete lineage sorting obscure early supergroup splits [4, 14, 23].

To evaluate the phylogenetic topology, geological timing, and molecular constraints governing nuclear emergence, we combined an 18-locus universal informational and core cellular dataset across 64 archaeal and eukaryotic species with functional evolutionary analyses of the nuclear compartment itself [1, 12–19]. Specifically, we paired partitioned third-codon RY phylogenomics [14, 15], multi-locus quartet coalescent species-tree inference [17], four-taxon allele-sharing tests [19], and fossil-calibrated relaxed-clock dating [12, 16, 24] with codon-level selection models [18] across four core functional pillars of nuclear biology: the ESCRT-III membrane-remodeling ATPase VPS4 [2, 6], octameric nucleosomal Histone H3 [21], the RNA polymerase II catalytic subunit RPB2 [7, 9], and the nuclear transport switch RAN/GSP1 mapped directly onto crystallographic coordinates of GDP-bound Ran (PDB 1BYU) [11, 20], alongside intraspecific coalescent baselines across model archaeal and eukaryotic taxa.
section2_paragraphs: Across all 64 archaeal and eukaryotic target taxa, automated sequence curation and homology screening assembled an 18-partition supermatrix totaling 26,387 aligned nucleotide columns (23,975 parsimony-informative RY3 sites) spanning transcriptional subunits (*RPB1/rpoA1*, *RPB2/rpoB*), translation factors and universal ribosomal proteins (*EF1A/tuf*, *EF2/fusA*, *eIF5B/infB*, *uL2/RPL2*, *uL3/RPL3*, *uS3/RPS3*, *ThrRS*), DNA replication and repair enzymes (*RAD51/radA*, *FEN1*, *PCNA*), ER/plasma-membrane translocons (*Sec61A/SecY*), V/A-type rotary ATPases (*VMA1*, *VMA2*), group II chaperonins (*CCT*/thermosome), and structural SSU/LSU rRNAs [1, 4, 23]. Applying per-locus Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) model selection [14, 15] with edge-linked proportional partition rates and third-codon purine–pyrimidine (RY3) recoding reduced relative composition frequency variability by 83.6%—from RCFV = 0.1440 under unrecoded 4-state nucleotides and 0.1558 in unfiltered controls to RCFV = 0.0236—and improved model fit by Δln L = +8,013.34 units (ln L = −834,670.53 vs. −842,683.86 unpartitioned; ΔBIC = −14,265.4) across the 52 taxa meeting the ≥65% locus-completeness threshold [1, 14]. Mean ultrafast bootstrap support rose from 84.0% for single-locus SSU rRNA and 89.5% in unfiltered 64-taxon concatenations to 95.1% under partitioned RY3 inference (**Figures 1 & 2**; **Tables 3A, 3C & 3D**).

In the partitioned maximum-likelihood phylogeny, Euryarchaeota outgroups (`[A]`) root a monophyletic TACK + Asgard + Eukaryota clade (100% UFBoot2), within which TACK Proteoarchaeota (`[B]`) diverges sister to a monophyletic Asgardarchaeota + Eukaryota clade (100% UFBoot2) and crown Eukaryota (`[D]`–`[G]`) is separated from Asgardarchaeota (`[C]`) by a long, strongly supported stem branch (100% UFBoot2) [2–4, 23]. Constrained least-squares relaxed-clock dating (`TimeTreeLSD2`) [16] with parametric rate-and-Poisson bootstrap intervals places the Euryarchaeota root (**Node I**) in the Paleoarchean at 3,240.0 Ma (95% HPD: 3,097.8–3,487.5 Ma), the TACK–Asgard–Eukaryota divergence (**Node II**) at 3,083.4 Ma (2,820.9–3,337.7 Ma), the Asgard–FECA nuclear stem divergence (**Node III**) in the Neoarchean at 2,932.6 Ma (2,572.9–3,195.0 Ma), and the LECA crown radiation (**Node IV**) in the Paleoproterozoic at 1,853.6 Ma (1,594.4–2,113.6 Ma), followed by Mesoproterozoic–Phanerozoic crown radiations across SAR (**Node VIII**, 1,396.2 Ma), Dikarya Fungi (**Node VI**, 1,350.0 Ma), Dictyostelia (**Node V**, 1,095.6 Ma), and Embryophyta land plants (**Node VII**, 560.0 Ma) (**Figure 1**; **Table 2A**) [12, 13, 24–26].
section3_paragraphs: Because concatenated supermatrices exclude taxa below the 65% completeness threshold and can be misled by anomalous gene trees in rapid deep radiations, we inferred individual maximum-likelihood gene trees across all 18 universal partitions and reconciled all 64 archaeal and eukaryotic species under the Quartet Multispecies Coalescent (`runie-quartet-coalescent`) [1, 17]. Across 5,880,795 evaluated four-taxon gene-tree quartets, the species tree satisfied 4,295,693 quartets, yielding a normalized quartet concordance score of Q = 0.7305 under RY3 recoding (mean local posterior probability LPP = 0.8135) compared with Q = 0.4535 in unaligned zero-star negative controls (**Figure 3**; **Figure 6**; **Table 3A**).

Quartet decomposition confirms overwhelming multi-locus concordance for the primary domain and supergroup splits—including the archaeal root (q1 = 0.903, LPP = 1.00), TACK vs. Asgard + Eukarya (q1 = 0.779, LPP = 1.00), and the Asgard–LECA stem separating Asgardarchaeota from crown eukaryotes (q1 = 0.916, LPP = 1.00; 1.78 coalescent units)—while recovering all 12 Opisthokonta species (`[E]`) as a single monophyletic clade (**Table 2B**) [4, 17, 23]. Conversely, short internal branches (~0.02–0.15 CU) and elevated alternative quartet weights (~0.30–0.33) among early-diverging Discoba, Amoebozoa, and Diaphoretickes reflect genuine ancient incomplete lineage sorting during LECA supergroup divergence [24], whereas four-taxon Patterson's *D* contrasts (`ABBA-1` to `ABBA-4`, |Z| ≤ 1.38) detect symmetric background site sharing rather than recent cross-domain horizontal chimerism (**Table 2B**) [19].
section4_paragraphs: To test how selective pressures acted on the structural components that physically construct and operate the eukaryotic nucleus, we fitted 61-state Goldman–Yang codon substitution models (M0, M1a, M2a) [18] across 47 curated RefSeq mRNA orthologs spanning four nuclear-origin protein families (**Figure 5A–B**; **Table 4A**). Every family exhibited strong purifying constraint with zero positively selected codons (Bayes Empirical Bayes Pr ≥ 0.95 = 0 across all families; M2a vs. M1a LRT = 0.00): the ESCRT-III membrane-remodeling AAA+ ATPase VPS4 (`FAM-01`; N = 13, 355 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1006, κ = 1.83) [2, 6], core nucleosomal Histone H3 (`FAM-02`; N = 12, 136 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.0309, κ = 2.09) [21], the RNA polymerase II catalytic subunit RPB2 (`FAM-03`; N = 10, 480 core codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.0853, κ = 1.56) [7, 9], and the nuclear transport GTPase RAN/GSP1 (`FAM-04`; N = 12, 206 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.0314, κ = 1.91) [11, 20].

Three-dimensional homology threading of eukaryotic RAN (`Mus musculus` NM_009391, 216 aa; 99.0% sequence identity across 202 aligned residues) onto the 2.15 Å crystal structure of mammalian Ran-GDP (PDB `1BYU` Chain A) [11] yielded near-identical backbone geometry (Kabsch Cα RMSD = 0.94 Å, TM-score = 0.9782) around a 594.9 Å³ nucleotide-binding pocket (estimated GDP affinity −6.95 kcal/mol; **Figure 5D**). Complete sequence invariance across eukaryotic supergroups locks the Walker A phosphate-binding P-loop (`GDGGTGKT`, residues 17–24), the Switch II catalytic glutamine motif (`DTAGQE`, residues 66–71), the `NKVD` guanine-specificity loop (residues 122–125), and the 2.32 Å octahedral coordination bond between Thr24 Oγ1 and `MG A 221`—preserving the conformational nucleotide switch required for karyopherin cargo import and export across Nuclear Pore Complexes [8, 9, 11, 20].
section5_paragraphs: To benchmark how these conserved informational and cytoskeletal markers behave at the population level within extant archaeal and eukaryotic species, we reconstructed 12 single-species Bayesian coalescent skylines (25,000 MCMC generations, 20% burn-in) strictly separated by species and homologous locus (**Figures 4A & 4B**; **Table 4B**) [1]. Axis A (`R1`–`R6`) contrasts diploid eukaryotic translation elongation factor `EF1A` cohorts in *Cryptococcus neoformans* (`R1`), *Fusarium oxysporum* (`R2`), *Giardia intestinalis* (`R3`), and *Danio rerio* (`R4`) against haploid archaeal 16S rRNA in *Haloferax volcanii* (`R5`) and nuclear 18S rRNA in *Chlamydomonas reinhardtii* (`R6`). Axis B (`L1`–`L6`) pairs single-copy coding RNA polymerase II `RPB2` (*F. oxysporum* `L1`, *C. neoformans* `L3`) and actin `ACT1` (*Saccharomyces cerevisiae* `L6`) directly against secondary-structure-guided (`mafft-native` E-INS-i) nuclear 18S rRNA skylines in *S. cerevisiae* (`L2`), *Oryza sativa* (`L4`), and *Paramecium tetraurelia* (`L5`).

Across homologous coding and ribosomal alignments, gap-consistent site-frequency summaries recover realistic intraspecific nucleotide diversity and neutral-to-purifying Tajima's *D* regimes, while minimum-spanning and TCS haplotype clustering (`Stage 3C`; **Figure 7A**; **Table 4C**) partitions *EF1A/tuf* (`Panel A`) into six multi-haplotype clusters separated by explicit interspecific mutational bridges without edge crossings, whereas the single-cluster *RPB2/rpoB* cohort (`Panel B`, 1 cluster; below the three-cluster graphical inclusion threshold) is summarized in **Table 4C** [1].
manuscript_prose.section6_intro: Quantitative sequence-hygiene logs, fossil-calibrated divergence estimates with quartet concordance metrics, clade recovery and four-taxon ABBA–BABA tests, 4-regime and 32-chain substitution model comparisons, per-locus BIC rate multipliers, Goldman–Yang codon selection parameters, and single-species coalescent skyline summaries are compiled in **Tables 1–4C** below [1, 14–19].
